ety.text: From Old French estaise (“ecstasy, rapture”), from Latin ecstasis, from Ancient Greek ἔκστασις (ékstasis), from ἐξίστημι (exístēmi, “to displace”), from ἐκ (ek, “out”) and ἵστημι (hístēmi, “to stand”).

ex: He loved me well, and oft would beg me sing; / Which when I did, he on the tender grass / Would sit, and hearken even to ecstasy,

senses.d: A state of emotion so intense that a person is carried beyond rational thought and self-control.
ex: They were thrown into ecstasies of suspicion by finding that we possessed a French translation of Hitler's Mein Kampf.

senses.d: A trance, frenzy, or rapture associated with mystic or prophetic exaltation.
ex: What! are you dreaming, Son! with Eyes cast upwards / Like a mad Prophet in an Ecstasy?

senses.d: Violent emotion or distraction of mind; excessive grief from anxiety; insanity; madness.
ex: Come, let us leave him; in his ireful mood / Our words will but increase his ecstasy.

senses.d: The drug MDMA, a synthetic entactogen of the methylenedioxyphenethylamine family, especially in a tablet form.
A state in which sensibility, voluntary motion, and (largely) mental power are suspended, and the body is erect and inflexible.
ex: The instant I drew out my case of instruments, the lady roused herself from her ecstasy, and has never had a similar attack.

grp.label: trance associated with mystic or prophetic exaltation
